# *Next Lives Here.*

The University of Cincinnati's Department of **Mechanical, Materials, and Industrial Engineering (MMIE)** is a research-intensive home for engineers who want to build things that matter — from high-temperature alloys for jet engines to smart manufacturing systems for the factory floor. Located inside CEAS, the college that invented cooperative education, MMIE graduates leave ready to lead.

[Explore Graduate Programs →](https://www.ceas.uc.edu/academics/departments/mechanical-materials-engineering/degrees-programs.html){.btn .btn-primary}
[Partner with MMIE →](https://www.ceas.uc.edu/research.html){.btn .btn-secondary}

::::

## Why UC? A Legacy of Firsts

![Mantei Engineering Research Center, home of the College of Engineering and Applied Science, on UC's main campus. *Photo by Warren LeMay. License: CC BY-SA 2.0.*](/files/photos/Capabilities/52955411548_a088cd4b39_c.jpg){.img-full fig-alt="Mantei Engineering Research Center, University of Cincinnati, CUF, Cincinnati, OH. Photo by Warren LeMay, 6 May 2023. License: CC BY-SA 2.0"}

The University of Cincinnati was founded in **1819** and today enrolls **`{python} d['uc_facts']['enrollment']`** students across three campuses.  Its Carnegie R1 designation reflects a sustained commitment to high-impact research.

```{python}
#| label: highlights-list
#| output: asis

items = "\n".join(f"- {h}" for h in d["highlights"])
print(items)
```

Herman Schneider's "Cincinnati Plan" — launched in 1906 from what is now CEAS — pioneered a model of paid, full-time work rotations integrated directly into degree programs.  That same ethos shapes how MMIE faculty approach research partnerships today: industry sponsors don't just write checks, they co-create knowledge alongside students and faculty.

## Research in MMIE

```{python}
#| label: research-areas
#| output: asis

areas = d["research_areas"]
mid  = len(areas) // 2

col1 = "\n".join(f"- {a}" for a in areas[:mid])
col2 = "\n".join(f"- {a}" for a in areas[mid:])

print(f"""
:::{{.columns}}
::{{.column width="50%"}}
{col1}
::
::{{.column width="50%"}}
{col2}
::
:::
""")
```

Research in MMIE is organized around **`{python} d['mmie_facts']['research_centers']` major centers** and more than a dozen specialized laboratories.  Signature themes include:

**Advanced Manufacturing** — MMIE is a regional leader in additive manufacturing research, including gas-phase alloying and sintering kinetics of 3D-printed metals and magnetic-field assisted laser metal deposition of oriented nickel superalloys.  The college's Digital Fabrication Laboratory supports both fundamental science and technology-transfer projects.

**Materials Characterization & Modeling** — High-resolution TEM, thermomechanical testing, electron backscatter diffraction, CALPHAD-based thermodynamic and kinetic modeling, and phase-field simulation capabilities allow faculty to study materials from the atomic scale up.

**Energy & Nuclear Materials** — Growing investments in high temperature alloy performance, metals process modeling, rare-earth-free magnet materials, and energy device materials connect MMIE to national laboratory, Department of Defense, and Department of Energy priorities.

**Smart Systems & Industry 4.0/5.0** — Faculty in dynamics, controls, structural health monitoring, and data analytics partner with regional manufacturers to deploy AI-driven inspection and process-optimization tools.

## Degree Programs

#| label: degree-table
#| output: asis

rows = "\n".join(f"| {deg} |" for deg in d["degree_list"])

| Program |

Graduate students in MMIE have access to the full breadth of CEAS facilities, a rich seminar series, and UC's professional-development infrastructure.  Many research assistantships are funded through external grants from NSF, DOE, DOD/AFRL, and industrial sponsors.


## Industry & Sponsor Engagement

```{python}
#| label: partner-logos
#| output: asis

partners = d["industry_partners"]
badges = "  ".join(f"`{p}`{{.badge}}" for p in partners)
print(f"> **Current and recent industrial partners include:** {badges}")
```

MMIE's industrial engagement model mirrors the broader UC co-op philosophy: deep, long-term relationships rather than transactional sponsorships.  Mechanisms for engagement include:

- **Sponsored Research Agreements** — fund specific graduate student projects with IP rights negotiated upfront.
- **Consortium Research** — cost-shared access to pre-competitive results (contact the CEAS Research Office).
- **Student Talent Pipeline** — co-op rotations and direct-hire relationships with graduating M.S./Ph.D. students.
- **Shared-Use Facilities** — external access to the Cleanroom, characterization instruments, and computational clusters.

> "Our research agenda at the University of Cincinnati has grown incredibly, thanks to the talents of our faculty researchers and their passion for discovery."  
> — **Neville Pinto, PhD**, President, University of Cincinnati

For sponsorship inquiries, contact the [CEAS Research Office](https://www.ceas.uc.edu/research.html).


## Cincinnati: A City Built for Engineers

![Cincinnati viewed from Devou Park in Covington, KY. *Photo by Ynsalh. License: CC BY-SA 4.0.*](/files/photos/Capabilities/Cincinnati_Skyline_from_Devou_Park.jpg){.img-full fig-alt="Cincinnati viewed from Devou Park in Covington, KY, by Ynsalh. License: CC BY-SA 4.0."}

Cincinnati is home to a dense cluster of advanced-manufacturing and aerospace companies, giving MMIE researchers unmatched access to real-world problems and industry networking.  The city's cost of living is well below coastal research hubs, and students' co-op earnings substantially offset the costs of tuition.
